title: Star of David Emoji ✡️ Meaning: Jewish Identity and Faith
description: The Star of David emoji ✡️ is the six-pointed Magen David of Jewish identity, used for holidays, Shabbat and remembrance. See how it differs from 🔯 and 🇮🇱.
summary: The ✡️ Star of David emoji shows the six-pointed Magen David, the best-known symbol of Jewish identity and of Judaism. Jewish users post it for Shabbat, holidays like Hanukkah and Passover, bar and bat mitzvahs, and pride in their heritage. Others use it in interfaith greetings and in Holocaust remembrance.
meaning: ✡️ represents the Jewish people and the Jewish faith. Its Hebrew name, Magen David, means "shield of David," after the biblical king. In a profile or caption it usually states identity: the person is Jewish, observant or secular, and proud of it. It is used across denominations and by Jews who are not religious, since the symbol speaks to peoplehood as much as belief.

The hexagram is ancient as a decorative shape, but its role as the emblem of the Jewish community grew over centuries, became widespread in the 1800s, and was adopted by the Zionist movement in 1897. It now appears on synagogues, gravestones, jewelry and the flag of Israel. Under Nazi rule Jews were forced to wear a yellow star, so the symbol also carries the memory of the Holocaust.

Online the emoji marks Jewish life and its calendar: "Shabbat shalom ✡️" on Friday afternoons, wishes for Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur, Hanukkah candle photos, Passover seders. It also appears in posts about antisemitism and in remembrance on Yom HaShoah and International Holocaust Remembrance Day. Synagogues and Jewish schools add it to event notices and calendars.

Christians sometimes use ✡️ respectfully in interfaith messages, in greetings to Jewish friends, or when writing about the Jewish roots of Christianity. It is not a general star or a decorative sparkle, and using it that way can confuse or offend. Users who want a sparkle should choose ⭐ or ✨ instead, and those writing about the State of Israel usually reach for its flag.

contexts.label: On Jewish holidays
contexts.body: ✡️ joins greetings for Rosh Hashanah, Yom Kippur, Sukkot, Hanukkah, Purim and Passover, often next to 🕎 for Hanukkah or 🍷 for the seder. Weekly, many people post "Shabbat shalom ✡️" before sundown on Friday. Community centers and synagogues use it in event announcements.

contexts.label: In bios and captions
contexts.body: A ✡️ in a profile signals Jewish identity, sometimes alongside 🇮🇱 or a hometown flag for diaspora communities. Celebrities and athletes use it to mark their heritage. Because Jewish identity is both religious and ethnic, the symbol appears on profiles of observant and secular people alike.

contexts.label: In interfaith and remembrance posts
contexts.body: Churches, schools and public figures add ✡️ to Holocaust remembrance messages, statements against antisemitism, and interfaith greetings that list several religious symbols together. In those settings it should be used with care and seriousness, with the date or occasion named so the purpose is clear.

confusedWith.difference: 🔯 is a six-pointed star with a dot in the center, from the Japanese emoji set, linked to fortune-telling and astrology. It is not a Jewish symbol. ✡️ is the Star of David.
🇮🇱 is the flag of the State of Israel, which features a blue Star of David. ✡️ is a religious and cultural symbol of Jews everywhere and does not by itself refer to the country or its politics.
🕎 is the nine-branched Hanukkah menorah, used almost only for that holiday. ✡️ is the all-year symbol of Jewish identity.

avoid: Do not use ✡️ as a generic star or decoration; ⭐ or ✨ is what you want.
Avoid using it to stand for Israeli government policy; it represents Jewish people broadly.
Never use it in jokes about the Holocaust or in mocking contexts.
design: Two overlapping equilateral triangles forming a six-pointed star. On Apple, Google and most other platforms it is drawn in white on the purple tile used for religious symbols. The character is an older text dingbat, so in some fonts it appears as a plain outline star without a tile. Designs do not vary in any meaningful way.

faqs.q: Is ✡️ the same as the Israeli flag?
faqs.a: No. The flag of Israel includes a Star of David, but the emoji itself represents Jews and Judaism worldwide. Many Jewish users live outside Israel and use ✡️ for their faith and heritage, not for a nation.

faqs.q: What is the difference between ✡️ and 🔯?
faqs.a: ✡️ is the Star of David, a Jewish symbol. 🔯 has a dot in the middle and came from Japanese phone emoji, where it was associated with fortune-telling. Use ✡️ for anything related to Judaism.

faqs.q: Can non-Jewish people use the Star of David emoji?
faqs.a: Yes, in respectful contexts: greeting Jewish friends on holidays, standing against antisemitism, or interfaith messages. It is best not used as decoration or in jokes, and it should not be used to stand for Jewish people in arguments.

faqs.q: Why is it called the Star of David?
faqs.a: It translates the Hebrew Magen David, "shield of David," named after the biblical king. The name links the shape to Jewish tradition, though the symbol became a widespread emblem of the community only in more recent centuries.
The symbol existed in Unicode as text long before emoji. It was given emoji presentation in 2014 and is listed under Emoji 0.7, along with several other religious symbols.
